scope: SCOPED: RFC8200 (STD 86) base IPv6 header encoder, parser and checked quoted-header codec: field widths, lengths, addresses and protocol selector, including Hop Limit zero and zero Payload Length differences. No full-document or full IPv6 host conformance: extension headers, fragmentation/reassembly, jumbograms, routing/forwarding, flow assignment, address administration and other full-host facilities are outside this inventory.

paragraphs.reason: The encoder writes version 6; live and checked quote parsers reject every other four-bit version, independently of traffic-class bits.

paragraphs.quote: Traffic Class 8-bit Traffic Class field. See Section 7.
paragraphs.reason: All 256 wire values round-trip without affecting version or flow-label bits. This traces field transport, not a complete traffic-management or DiffServ policy.

paragraphs.quote: Flow Label 20-bit flow label. See Section 6.
paragraphs.reason: The encoder initializes the 20-bit field to zero and the parser ignores it without contaminating the adjacent traffic-class field. Flow-label assignment and network flow treatment are not selected capabilities.

paragraphs.quote: Payload Length 16-bit unsigned integer. Length of the IPv6 payload, i.e., the rest of the packet following this IPv6 header, in octets. (Note that any extension headers (see Section 4) present are considered part of the payload, i.e., included in the length count.)
paragraphs.reason: Declared base-packet length is 40 plus the full unsigned 16-bit field, including zero; complete frames require exact bounds and checked quotes retain the original length when truncated. Extension headers, including Jumbo Payload options, remain explicitly unsupported under the existing scope.

paragraphs.quote: Next Header 8-bit selector. Identifies the type of header immediately following the IPv6 header. Uses the same values as the IPv4 Protocol field [IANA-PN].
paragraphs.reason: Encoder emits TCP protocol 6; parser and checked quotes expose the exact selector for non-extension protocols. Known extension/fragment selectors are rejected explicitly by the atomic parser and quote decoder; only the separate fragment API admits a Fragment header. This field-format evidence does not claim extension traversal, unknown-protocol ICMP generation or full host demultiplexing; No Next Header processing is separately traced.

paragraphs.quote: Hop Limit 8-bit unsigned integer. Decremented by 1 by each node that forwards the packet. When forwarding, the packet is discarded if Hop Limit was zero when received or is decremented to zero. A node that is the destination of a packet should not discard a packet with Hop Limit equal to zero; it should process the packet normally.
paragraphs.reason: This destination codec preserves all Hop Limit values, including zero, while checking structure and declared length. Forwarding and decrement rules remain outside the existing endpoint scope; originating parameter policy is unchanged.

paragraphs.quote: Source Address 128-bit address of the originator of the packet. See [RFC4291].
paragraphs.reason: Distinct full-width address octets are encoded and decoded in network order, including checked quotes. Address assignment and RFC4291 host semantics are not claimed.

paragraphs.quote: Destination Address 128-bit address of the intended recipient of the packet (possibly not the ultimate recipient, if a Routing header is present). See [RFC4291] and Section 4.4.
paragraphs.reason: The complete base-header address field is preserved by encode, parse and checked quotes. The routing qualification is retained in the quotation: routing-header processing and ultimate-destination derivation are unsupported, not claimed by this direct base-field codec evidence.

paragraphs.quote: The value 59 in the Next Header field of an IPv6 header or any extension header indicates that there is nothing following that header. If the Payload Length field of the IPv6 header indicates the presence of octets past the end of a header whose Next Header field contains 59, those octets must be ignored and passed on unchanged if the packet is forwarded.
paragraphs.reason: For base selector 59, empty and positive-length packets expose no transport payload after exact declared-bound checks; the borrowed input bytes and quoted length/protocol remain intact. Extension traversal and forwarding remain outside the existing endpoint scope.

paragraphs.quote: A full implementation of IPv6 includes implementation of the following extension headers: Hop-by-Hop Options Fragment Destination Options Routing Authentication Encapsulating Security Payload
paragraphs.reason: Explicit full-host boundary: the selected codec rejects these headers, except that its fragment API parses and encodes a Fragment header directly after the base header, and does not claim a full IPv6 implementation. This context is not an exception closing a selected base-header defect. Host fragmentation/reassembly, routing, security headers and jumbograms remain unsupported.

paragraphs.quote: The current use of the Traffic Class field for Differentiated Services and Explicit Congestion Notification is specified in [RFC2474] and [RFC3168].
paragraphs.reason: Section 3's field-format evidence does not establish these complete external policies; the selected sticky TCP ECN override is traced under RFC3542.

paragraphs.quote: The current definition of the IPv6 Flow Label can be found in [RFC6437].
paragraphs.reason: Only the base field's width, zero emission and isolation are selected; flow-label assignment and network treatment are outside this inventory.
